back: A disease that must by law be reported to the veterinary services when suspected.

front: Anthrax: cause, sign and key rule
back: Spore-forming bacterium; sudden death with dark unclotted blood from openings; never open the carcass, report it.
Virus of cloven-hoofed animals; blisters on mouth, feet and teats, drooling, lameness; control by quarantine, movement control and vaccination.
Viral disease of poultry; gasping, twisted neck, green diarrhoea, egg drop, deaths; prevent by vaccination.
Protozoan blood disease spread by tsetse flies; anaemia and wasting; control tsetse and use trypanocidal drugs.
Natural active (recovery), artificial active (vaccination), natural passive (colostrum), artificial passive (antiserum).
The first milk after birth, rich in antibodies; must be sucked within the first few hours.
Active: own antibodies, slow to start, long-lasting. Passive: borrowed antibodies, immediate, lasts only weeks.
Killed or weakened pathogens (or parts) that make an animal produce its own antibodies without getting the disease.
